correctness.rationale: Militaru 2026 Theorem 2.12, Corollary 2.13 and Proposition 2.15 give the exact orbit model and stabilizer interpretation for nonsplit bipartite solutions. With m=|Z| and k=n-m, m! choices in each tuple position, orbit counts lie between T/m! and T, T=binom(m!+k-1,k). Stirling then gives F_n=m(n-m)(log m-1)+O(n log n) on m in [n/3,2n/3]; strict saddle concavity yields x=m/n=1/2+1/(4log n)+O((log n)^-2) and maximal log term n²/(16log n). For typical m,k~n/2, Burnside fixed-point sum over S_m×S_k is asymptotically identity-only: permutations with f fixed tuple coordinates contribute at most |C_beta|^f (m!)^((k-f)/2), and every nontrivial S_m conjugacy class has size ≥m(m-1)/2. The resulting error tends to zero, so typical orbit stabilizers are trivial and o(m,k)~(m!)^(k-1)/k!, producing the asymptotic weighted sum. Independently computed finite saddle displacement for n=400,2000,10000 and checked prior enumeration; finite tests are not the proof of Burnside asymptotics.
